lines: What is Intentional Injury Crime? By its legal definition, intentional injury is any unlawful act that causes pain to another person's body or impairs their health or perception ability. The legislator addresses the protected interest under three headings: causing bodily pain (a physical blow such as slapping or kicking), impairing health (leading to anatomical or psychological disorder), and impairing perception ability (temporarily or permanently disrupting consciousness or rational thought, for example, by intoxicating with excessive alcohol).

lines: Difference Between Simple Injury and Severe Injury The first level determining the perpetrator's sentence is the forensic report obtained from the Forensic Medicine Institute or a fully equipped hospital. If the injury is not of a magnitude that can be healed with a simple dressing or first aid, the basic form of the crime occurs, and imprisonment from 1 year to 3 years is applied in accordance with the first paragraph of Article 86 of the Turkish Penal Code; this crime is not subject to complaint.

lines: If results such as a permanent weakening of the function of a sense or organ, permanent speech impairment, a permanent scar on the face, or the premature birth of a pregnant woman's child occur, the basic penalty is increased by onefold. lines: Does the Case Drop if the Complaint is Withdrawn? The rule is based on a clear distinction. The case drops only if the injury can be remedied with a simple medical intervention (Turkish Penal Code m.86/2) and none of the aggravating circumstances (such as with a weapon, against an official, against a spouse) are present when the victim withdraws the complaint. The period for making a complaint is 6 months from the incident.

lines: Summary In a building declared a risky structure, decisions regarding reconstruction, contractor selection, and sharing can now be made not by a two-thirds majority, but by a simple majority (50%+1) of apartment owners calculated based on their land shares. A 15-day notice is sent to minority owners who do not agree to the decision via a notary; if the agreement is not signed within this period, their land shares are put up for auction. If the majority's decision is unfair, minority owners can file a nullification lawsuit in the Civil Court of Peace.

lines: Could a Single Neighbor's Refusal to Sign Have Delayed the Entire Building for Years? In the past, when a building requiring renewal due to earthquake risk, the refusal of a single owner or a small minority to sign could stall the project for years. The amendment to the law prevented this gridlock; however, in the new system, strict procedural rules and minority protection mechanisms have been introduced to ensure that the majority does not victimize the minority.

lines: This guide addresses how a simple majority decision is reached, the meeting and notification process, the rights of minority owners, and the procedure for selling the land shares of those who refrain from signing.

lines: What is a Simple Majority Decision? Under the old regulation, applications following the demolition of a building declared a risky structure required a two-thirds majority of stakeholders. According to current legislation, all decisions such as the reconstruction of the immovable property, contractor selection, terms of the construction contract, and sharing principles can now be made by a simple majority (50%+1) of apartment owners calculated based on their land shares. This ratio is calculated not based on the number of people but on the land share ratio in the title deed. The purpose of the regulation is to prevent a single owner or a small minority from halting the transformation process of an entire building for years.

This ratio is calculated not based on the number of people but on the land share ratio in the title deed. The purpose of the regulation is to prevent a single owner or a small minority from halting the transformation process of an entire building for years.

lines: Apartment Owners Meeting and Decision-Making Process The ability to make decisions by simple majority is strictly tied to the formal requirements stipulated by law. After the risky structure determination becomes final, one of the owners or the building management sends a meeting invitation to all apartment owners via a notary or registered mail; the invitation must clearly specify the location, time, and agenda of the meeting. In the meeting, the group that achieves a simple majority of land shares signs a decision protocol regarding how the transformation will be carried out and with which construction company an agreement will be made.

lines: To minority owners who did not attend the meeting or opposed the decision, the adopted decision and draft contract are served via a notary. The warning states that the decision must be joined within 15 days from its notification, otherwise the land shares will be sold by auction.

lines: Rights of the Minority Not Joining the Decision The power of the simple majority to make decisions is not absolute. If the decision taken is contrary to the rule of honesty, if an unfair distribution of shares has been made to the minority (e.g., valuable facades given only to the majority group), the owner whose right has been infringed can file a lawsuit in the Civil Court of Peace for the annulment of the decision and the suspension of the project; abuse of right is not protected in law.

lines: Case Summary A 10-apartment building with equal land shares was declared a risky structure and demolished. Six of the owners (60% of the shares) want to sign a construction contract in exchange for apartments, while the remaining four owners refrain from signing because they do not like the project.

lines: Legal Assessment Since the 60% share provides the simple majority condition, the decision is legally valid. lines: Legal Assessment This situation is clearly contrary to the rule of honesty and the principle of equality. lines: Sale of Land Shares of Owners Who Refrain from Signing The land shares of owners who do not sign the contract despite the 15-day warning sent to them are put up for auction by the Provincial Directorate of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change. Only other apartment owners in the building can participate in this auction; the sale is made to the highest bidder at a price not less than the market value determined by the licensed company. If other co-owners do not buy the share, the land share is expropriated by the Ministry or registered in the name of the Treasury and transferred to the contractor, provided that the market value is paid; this prevents the project from stopping.

Conditions, Time Limits, and Critical Differences Under Articles 344, 345, and 138 of the Turkish Code of Obligations (TCO). lines: Summary: A rent assessment case is filed to redetermine the current rent based on comparable market values; as a rule, 5 years must pass from the contract date, and a lawsuit must be filed or a warning issued at least 30 days before the new period. A rent adaptation case, on the other hand, can be filed at any time, without any time limit, if an unforeseen extraordinary development occurs after the contract is established. Both types of lawsuits require the mandatory mediation process to be exhausted before filing.

lines: Two Different Cases, Two Different Stories: A landlord whose rent is far below market value and a tenant who becomes unable to pay rent due to an unexpected crisis should, in fact, resort to two completely different legal paths. These two types of cases are often confused, and filing the wrong type of lawsuit can lead to the outright rejection of a process that could take years.

lines: This guide discusses the conditions, timing, and fundamental differences between rent assessment cases and rent adaptation cases.

lines: What is a Rent Assessment Case? A rent assessment case is a type of lawsuit that allows the judge to redetermine the current rent for a new rental period, taking into account the location, characteristics, and comparable market values of the property. Its legal basis is Articles 344 and 345 of the Turkish Code of Obligations.
kira-tespit-ve-uyarlama-davalari-rehberi.text: What is a Rent Assessment Case? A rent assessment case is a type of lawsuit that allows the judge to redetermine the current rent for a new rental period, taking into account the location, characteristics, and comparable market values of the property. Its legal basis is Articles 344 and 345 of the Turkish Code of Obligations.

lines: For the case to be filed, there must be a valid and ongoing residential or roofed workplace rental agreement between the parties. Pursuant to the third paragraph of Article 344 of the Law, the determination of a new rent can be requested in rental agreements exceeding 5 years or renewed after 5 years. In cases filed within the first 5 years, the judge determines an increase that does not exceed the twelve-month average change rate in the consumer price index. In cases filed after 5 years, this limit is removed, and the determination is made directly based on current comparable values, applying an equity reduction.

In cases filed after 5 years, this limit is removed, and the determination is made directly based on current comparable values, applying an equity reduction.

lines: A rent assessment case can, as a rule, be filed at any time; however, for the case to affect the new period, it must be filed at least 30 days before the start of the new period, or a written warning from the landlord regarding a rent increase must have been served to the tenant within this period. If this condition is met, the new amount determined by the court will be valid from the first day of the new period; otherwise, the case will take effect for the subsequent rental period.

If this condition is met, the new amount determined by the court will be valid from the first day of the new period; otherwise, the case will take effect for the subsequent rental period.

lines: What is a Rent Adaptation Case? A rent adaptation case is filed to adapt the contract to new conditions if radical developments occur after the contract's establishment that could not have been foreseen by the parties and would be contrary to the rule of good faith. Its legal basis is Article 138 of the Turkish Code of Obligations, which regulates excessive difficulty in performance.
kira-tespit-ve-uyarlama-davalari-rehberi.text: What is a Rent Adaptation Case? A rent adaptation case is filed to adapt the contract to new conditions if radical developments occur after the contract's establishment that could not have been foreseen by the parties and would be contrary to the rule of good faith. Its legal basis is Article 138 of the Turkish Code of Obligations, which regulates excessive difficulty in performance.

lines: Four conditions are required for the case to be filed: an extraordinary situation (such as an economic crisis, pandemic, natural disaster) that did not exist when the contract was made must arise; it must have been impossible to foresee this situation when the contract was signed; the performance of the party's obligation must have reached a level contrary to the rule of good faith due to the changed circumstances; and the party whose right is harmed must not yet have performed their obligation or must have paid it with a reservation, stating "I reserve my rights." The adaptation request of a party who continues to pay unconditionally is weakened.

The adaptation request of a party who continues to pay unconditionally is weakened.

lines: In a rent adaptation case, there is no waiting period as in an assessment case. If extraordinary and unforeseen conditions occur even in the first month of the contract, the case can be filed immediately; it is not dependent on any periodic calendar or warning condition.

lines: Mandatory Mediation Requirement: Pursuant to the regulation made under Law No. 7445, it is mandatory to apply to a mediation office before filing both rent assessment cases and rent adaptation cases. Cases filed directly without exhausting the mediation stage will be rejected by the court on procedural grounds. Furthermore, filing an adaptation case when an assessment case should be filed, or vice versa, leads to the rejection of the case and the burden of unnecessary attorney fees.

lines: Can a tenant also file a rent assessment case? Rarely, yes. Although this case is usually filed by the landlord to increase the rent, in exceptional circumstances where market conditions cause the rent to be excessively high, the tenant can also file an assessment case to request a reduction.

lines: Is the right to sue completely lost if the 30-day warning period is missed? No, a lawsuit can always be filed; however, if the time limit is not met, the new amount determined by the court will not be valid for the current period but for the subsequent rental period. Therefore, tracking the deadline directly affects the magnitude of the loss.

maas-ve-banka-hesabi-haczi-nasil-kaldiri.text: How to Lift a Salary and Bank Account Attachment (Garnishment)? Legal Limits Under Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law Articles 83 and 89, Methods of Lifting E-Attachment. This guide has been updated as of 2026, based on the Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law No. 2004.

lines: Summary: A maximum of one-fourth of an employee's salary can be attached; this limit does not apply to alimony debts, and current month's alimony is deducted entirely from the salary. SGK retirement pensions cannot be attached without the debtor's consent; a block placed on these accounts is unlawful and can be lifted by objecting to the enforcement office. An attachment placed on a bank account automatically falls (lapses) if the debt is paid, an installment commitment is made under Article 111 of the EBL, or if the money is not requested to be transferred to the file within 1 year from the date of the attachment.

lines: Can a Block Be Placed on a Retirement Pension? Often No. Many individuals facing enforcement proceedings believe that an e-attachment (e-haciz) placed on their account is a final and unchallengeable action. However, the law has imposed strict limits on salaries and certain types of accounts to protect the debtor's minimum living conditions. Especially a block placed on retirement pension accounts is often directly unlawful and can be lifted with a quick objection.

lines: This guide addresses the legal limits of salary attachment, methods of lifting bank account attachment (e-attachment), and commonly encountered irregularities.

lines: Legal Limits of Salary Attachment: Pursuant to Article 83 of the Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law No. 2004, a debtor's salary or wage cannot be entirely attached. A maximum of one-fourth of the salary or wage received by the debtor can be attached; commitments made before the enforcement proceeding becomes final, aiming to attach the entire salary, are legally invalid.

A maximum of one-fourth of the salary or wage received by the debtor can be attached; commitments made before the enforcement proceeding becomes final, aiming to attach the entire salary, are legally invalid.

lines: The most critical exception to this rule is alimony debts: current month's alimony ordered by the court is deducted entirely from the salary, regardless of the one-fourth limit. For other debts, only one-fourth of the remaining salary can be deducted.

lines: If more than one salary attachment writ is received for the debtor, they are placed in order. The deduction by a subsequent enforcement office cannot begin before the previous attachment is completed; attachments cannot be combined to deduct more than one-fourth from the salary.

lines: How to Lift a Bank Account Attachment (E-Attachment)? The creditor can send an attachment notice to the debtor's bank accounts under Article 89 of the Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law or directly apply e-attachment electronically. There are several legal ways to lift this attachment.
maas-ve-banka-hesabi-haczi-nasil-kaldiri.text: How to Lift a Bank Account Attachment (E-Attachment)? The creditor can send an attachment notice to the debtor's bank accounts under Article 89 of the Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law or directly apply e-attachment electronically. There are several legal ways to lift this attachment.

lines: The most definitive way is to fully pay the file debt into the enforcement office's account. If the debtor cannot pay the entire debt at once, they can make a formal installment commitment to the enforcement office under Article 111 of the Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law; provided that the first installment is paid upfront and the remaining debt is paid in a maximum of 3 months in 4 equal installments, this commitment ensures the suspension of the attachment regardless of the creditor's consent.
maas-ve-banka-hesabi-haczi-nasil-kaldiri.text: The most definitive way is to fully pay the file debt into the enforcement office's account. If the debtor cannot pay the entire debt at once, they can make a formal installment commitment to the enforcement office under Article 111 of the Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law; provided that the first installment is paid upfront and the remaining debt is paid in a maximum of 3 months in 4 equal installments, this commitment ensures the suspension of the attachment regardless of the creditor's consent.

lines: Pursuant to Article 93 of Law No. 5510, SGK retirement pensions, disability pensions, and unemployment benefits cannot be attached without the debtor's consent (except for alimony and SGK premium debts). If a bank has placed a block on an account where a retirement pension is deposited, based on an e-attachment decision from an enforcement office, this action is clearly unlawful. The debtor should apply to the relevant enforcement office with a statement proving the account is a retirement pension account and request the block be lifted; if the request is denied, a complaint lawsuit must be filed with the Enforcement Court within 7 days.

lines: After an enforcement office places an attachment on a bank account, the creditor must request the transfer of this money to the enforcement file within legal periods. If the transfer of money in a movable bank account to the enforcement file is not requested within 1 year from the date of attachment, the attachment on the account legally falls (lapses), and the debtor can request the enforcement office to lift the attachment due to this expiration of time.

lines: A guide to the termination and liquidation of inheritance partnership under the Turkish Civil Code (TMK) articles 640-642, 644, and 698-699. This guide has been prepared based on the provisions of the Turkish Civil Code and the Law on Mediation in Legal Disputes, which are in force as of 2026.
miras-ortakliginin-giderilmesi-rehberi.text: A guide to the termination and liquidation of inheritance partnership under the Turkish Civil Code (TMK) articles 640-642, 644, and 698-699. This guide has been prepared based on the provisions of the Turkish Civil Code and the Law on Mediation in Legal Disputes, which are in force as of 2026.

lines: Upon the death of a testator, if there is more than one heir, a partnership arises over the estate, known as joint ownership (elbirliği mülkiyeti), which requires all heirs to act together. In this partnership, no heir can independently sell or dispose of their share; all heirs have rights over the entire estate jointly. Heirs can agree among themselves to divide the estate, or if they cannot agree, they can request the court to partition the inheritance. This process is commonly known in practice as “the lawsuit for the dissolution of partnership” or, by its old name, “izale-i şuyu lawsuit,” and since 2023, it is mandatory to go through a mediation phase before filing the lawsuit. Proper execution of the process prevents both unnecessary loss of time and the dismissal of the lawsuit due to lack of a prerequisite for legal action.

lines: 1. What is Inheritance Partnership (Joint Ownership)? In every inheritance with more than one heir, joint ownership is established over the estate upon the death of the testator, pursuant to TMK art. 640. In this type of ownership, heirs do not have specific, separate shares; all heirs have rights over the entire estate jointly, and disposition transactions can only be made unanimously. Unlike co-ownership (paylı mülkiyet), joint ownership does not allow one heir to independently sell or transfer their share; therefore, inheritance partnership is a legal situation that frequently leads to disputes in practice regarding the actual use and management of immovable properties.

lines: 2. Methods to Be Followed for the Dissolution of Partnership There are two main ways to terminate an inheritance partnership. The first way is for the heirs to agree among themselves and enter into an inheritance partition agreement; in this case, title deed transfer and sharing procedures can be carried out without the need for a lawsuit. If an agreement cannot be reached, any heir may request the civil court of peace (sulh hukuk mahkemesi) to partition the assets in the estate in kind, or if not possible, by sale, pursuant to TMK art. 642; this lawsuit is also referred to as an inheritance partition lawsuit in practice. Furthermore, TMK art. 644 grants heirs the right to request the conversion of joint ownership into co-ownership; in this case, the immovable property is first converted into co-ownership, and then it may become the subject of a classical lawsuit for the dissolution of partnership (izale-i şuyu) pursuant to TMK art. 698-699. The name under which the lawsuit is filed has no practical significance; legal qualification is the duty of the court, and the court examines the request by placing it on the correct legal basis.

lines: 3. Mandatory Mediation as a Prerequisite for Legal Action With the amendment introduced by Law No. 7445, which came into force on September 1, 2023, it has become a mandatory prerequisite for legal action to apply to a mediator before filing a lawsuit concerning disputes regarding the partition and dissolution of partnership of movable and immovable properties. If a direct application to the court is made after this date, the court will formally dismiss the lawsuit due to the absence of the prerequisite for legal action, without conducting any examination. The mediation process is completed within three weeks from the date of application, extendable by another week at the discretion of the mediator in mandatory cases, making a total of four weeks. Parties are obliged to attend mediation meetings but cannot be forced to agree; the process ends with an agreement or a failure to agree, and in both cases, a final report is drawn up. If an agreement is not reached, the original or a certified copy of this final report must be attached to the petition for the lawsuit; if not attached, the court will grant a definitive period of one week, and if not completed within this period, the lawsuit will be formally dismissed.

lines: 4. Competent and Authorized Court The competent court for a lawsuit for the dissolution of partnership is the civil court of peace. In terms of jurisdiction, the court where the immovable property is located has exclusive jurisdiction; parties cannot agree to file a lawsuit elsewhere. If the estate consists of immovable properties located in more than one province, a separate lawsuit must be filed for each immovable property in the civil court of peace where that immovable property is located. The lawsuit is subject to the simple trial procedure of the Code of Civil Procedure; in this procedure, the petition phase consists only of the plaintiff's petition and the defendant's response, and since there is no second petition phase, the process proceeds relatively faster.

lines: 5. Methods of Dissolution of Partnership: Partition in Kind and Partition by Sale When deciding on the dissolution of partnership, the court prioritizes partition in kind. In partition in kind, immovable properties in the estate are physically divided, if possible, in such a way that each is allocated to an heir; if there is a difference in value between the shares given to the heirs, this difference is equalized by a monetary payment (ivaz ilavesiyle). Partition in kind only comes into play if one of the parties requests it and if the immovable property is suitable for physical division in terms of its surface area, nature, and zoning status; for example, division into parcels smaller than five decares is not allowed in agricultural lands. Pursuant to Article 7 of the Condominium Law, in immovable properties where condominium ownership or construction servitude has been established, dissolution of partnership by sale is not possible. In cases where partition in kind is not possible or the immovable property would suffer a significant loss in value, the court decides on partition by sale; in this case, the immovable property is sold by auction according to the provisions of the Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law, and the proceeds are distributed among the co-owners proporcional to their inheritance shares.

lines: 6. Lawsuit Process and Parties In a lawsuit for the dissolution of partnership, it is mandatory for all heirs (co-owners) to be involved in the lawsuit; in the event of an incomplete formation of parties, the court grants a period to remedy the deficiency, and if not remedied, the lawsuit cannot be concluded formally. If one of the co-owners passes away during the trial, their heirs must be included in the lawsuit by obtaining a certificate of inheritance. This lawsuit is characterized as a "two-way lawsuit" in civil procedural law; there is no classical winner-loser relationship between the plaintiff and the defendant, and even if one party waives the lawsuit, another co-owner may request the continuation of the lawsuit. For this reason, litigation expenses are imposed on all parties proportionally to their ownership shares at the end of the lawsuit.

lines: CASE SUMMARY Mr. Nazım, who passed away leaving an apartment in Antalya and a summer house with a garden, had three children who could not agree on giving the apartment to themselves and the summer house to the youngest sibling. The eldest sibling, Mr. Selim, directly filed a lawsuit for the dissolution of partnership in the Civil Court of Peace to expedite the process, but did not attach the mediation final report to the petition.

The eldest sibling, Mr. Selim, directly filed a lawsuit for the dissolution of partnership in the Civil Court of Peace to expedite the process, but did not attach the mediation final report to the petition.

lines: APPLICATION AND LEGAL PROCESS The court, stating that mediation is a mandatory prerequisite for lawsuits filed after 2023, gave Mr. Selim a definitive period of one week to submit the final report. Thereupon, Mr. Selim's lawyer applied to the mediation office, and within three weeks, the siblings met; no agreement was reached on the apartment, but an agreement was reached to leave the summer house to the youngest sibling. The mediator recorded the partial agreement and the unresolved issues separately in the final report. Mr. Selim's lawyer attached this report to the lawsuit petition and only brought the claim regarding the apartment to the court. The court, as a result of expert examination, determined that the apartment could not be physically divided and decided on its partition by sale.

lines: OUTCOME The apartment was sold by auction, and the proceeds were distributed among the three siblings proportionally to their inheritance shares. The summer house, in accordance with the agreement reached in mediation, was registered in the land registry in the name of the youngest sibling without the need for a separate lawsuit. This process showed that partial agreement is possible in mediation and that only unresolved issues can be made subjects of a lawsuit.

As Küheylan Law Firm, our inheritance law department provides comprehensive legal support to our clients at every stage of the process, from estate determination to the management of the mediation process, from the preparation of the lawsuit petition to the follow-up of expert examination. If you are considering terminating your inheritance partnership, you can consult with our inheritance law team to complete the process with the correct steps and in the shortest time possible.

lines: Summary Alimony/Maintenance is regulated under four separate headings to maintain economic balance during the marriage and divorce process: provisional alimony/maintenance valid during the case, child support alimony/maintenance specific to the child, spousal support alimony/maintenance specific to the spouse, and assistance alimony/maintenance specific to the adult child. The amount determined by the court is not permanent; when there is a substantial change in the economic situation of the parties, a case for increase, decrease, or abolishment can be filed pursuant to TMK Art. 176. With the Constitutional Court's annulment of the phrase "indefinitely" in spousal support alimony/maintenance in 2026, this area has become one of the most litigated topics in the coming period.

lines: Why Does An Alimony/Maintenance Decision Not Stay The Same Forever? The amount of alimony/maintenance determined by the court is shaped by the economic conditions of the day it was issued. As time passes, inflation erodes alimony/maintenance, the income levels of the parties change, one remarries, one loses their job.

lines: The law does not ignore this reality: the amount of alimony/maintenance can be brought before the judiciary again when conditions change. The year 2026 marked a separate turning point in this area. The Constitutional Court annulled the provision stipulating that spousal support alimony/maintenance should be of indefinite nature. This decision concerns both existing alimony/maintenance creditors and debtors. Below are the types of alimony/maintenance, the conditions for an increase-decrease case, and the practical consequences of the 2026 decision.

lines: What Is Alimony/Maintenance, What Legal Articles Is It Based On? Alimony/maintenance is a regular payment made by a person to those they are legally obligated to support, in order to provide for their livelihood. The Turkish Civil Code regulates this payment not under a single article, but with different provisions depending on the situation: Article 195 of the Turkish Civil Code during the marriage, Articles 169, 175, and 182 of the Turkish Civil Code during and after divorce, and Article 364 of the Turkish Civil Code for adult children.

lines: The type of alimony/maintenance, the person in whose favor it will be awarded, and its amount are determined by the family court judge based on concrete facts such as the fault of the parties, income level, social status, and the child's best interests. That this decision is not “final and unchangeable” is the most critical feature of alimony/maintenance law.

lines: Provisional Alimony/Maintenance As soon as a divorce or separation case is filed, without waiting for the outcome of the case, the judge ex officio orders provisional alimony/maintenance for one of the parties and for the children, if any. The aim is to prevent the economically weaker spouse and children from suffering during the ongoing case. This type of alimony/maintenance is based on Articles 169 and 197 of the Turkish Civil Code.

lines: It automatically ends with the finalization of the divorce decision; it is replaced by child support or spousal support alimony/maintenance, depending on the situation.

lines: Child Support Alimony/Maintenance This is the alimony/maintenance paid by the non-custodial parent to the custodial parent as a contribution to the child's care, education, health, and housing expenses after divorce. It is regulated in Articles 182 and 329 of the Turkish Civil Code.

It is regulated in Articles 182 and 329 of the Turkish Civil Code.

lines: This alimony/maintenance is for the benefit of the child and is awarded independently of the parties' fault; even a faultless parent is obliged to pay. As a rule, it continues until the child turns 18; it can be converted into assistance alimony/maintenance for a child continuing their education.

lines: Spousal Support Alimony/Maintenance This is the type of alimony/maintenance that a spouse who will fall into economic hardship due to divorce and whose fault in the divorce is not heavier than the other party's, can claim in proportion to the financial strength of the other spouse, and it is regulated in Article 175 of the Turkish Civil Code. The law stipulated that this alimony/maintenance could be requested indefinitely; however, the Constitutional Court, with its General Assembly decision dated June 4, 2026, annulled the phrase "indefinitely" in the relevant article by a majority vote. The annulment provision will enter into force 9 months after its publication in the Official Gazette; the current regulation continues to be applied during this period. The Turkish Grand National Assembly is expected to make a new regulation connecting alimony/maintenance to an upper limit proportional to the marriage duration within this period. Finalized alimony/maintenance decisions are not retroactively affected by the annulment decision; after the effective date, new cases concerning the time limit will be opened.

lines: Assistance Alimony/Maintenance This is a type of alimony/maintenance not directly related to divorce, which can be claimed among relatives listed in the law (descendants, ascendants, and siblings who would fall into poverty if not assisted) and is based on Article 364 of the Turkish Civil Code. In practice, it is most often seen in the form of alimony/maintenance requested by an adult child continuing their education from their mother or father.

lines: Conditions for an Alimony/Maintenance Increase or Decrease Case Paragraph four of Article 176 of the Turkish Civil Code stipulates that if a "substantial change" occurs in the economic and social situation of the parties after the alimony/maintenance amount has been determined, the interested party may request the court to increase, decrease, or completely abolish the alimony/maintenance. The basic conditions required for the lawsuit to be accepted can be listed as follows.
nafaka-turleri-ve-artirim-azaltim-davasi.text: Conditions for an Alimony/Maintenance Increase or Decrease Case Paragraph four of Article 176 of the Turkish Civil Code stipulates that if a "substantial change" occurs in the economic and social situation of the parties after the alimony/maintenance amount has been determined, the interested party may request the court to increase, decrease, or completely abolish the alimony/maintenance. The basic conditions required for the lawsuit to be accepted can be listed as follows.

lines: The change must be substantial and concrete. A simple fluctuation in income is not sufficient; an increase or decrease in the poverty of the alimony/maintenance creditor, or a serious change in the debtor's payment capacity, must be proven with concrete evidence such as a salary slip, land registry record, or bank account statement.
nafaka-turleri-ve-artirim-azaltim-davasi.text: The change must be substantial and concrete. A simple fluctuation in income is not sufficient; an increase or decrease in the poverty of the alimony/maintenance creditor, or a serious change in the debtor's payment capacity, must be proven with concrete evidence such as a salary slip, land registry record, or bank account statement.

lines: The change must have occurred after the finalization of the decision. The alleged change cannot be a situation that the judge already knew or foresaw when the previous alimony/maintenance decision was made. The change is requested by filing a new lawsuit in the family court. It is not enough to submit a petition to the court that issued the previous decision; an objection to the enforcement file also does not produce this result.

lines: In spousal support alimony/maintenance, there are also grounds for termination. Remarriage of the alimony/maintenance creditor automatically terminates the alimony/maintenance; living with another person as if married, leading a dishonorable life, or acquiring a regular and sufficient income requires the abolishment of alimony/maintenance by court decision.

Remarriage of the alimony/maintenance creditor automatically terminates the alimony/maintenance; living with another person as if married, leading a dishonorable life, or acquiring a regular and sufficient income requires the abolishment of alimony/maintenance by court decision.

lines: For a request to increase child support alimony/maintenance, the child growing older and increased education expenses (private school, university, health expenses) are considered sufficient reasons alone. In a case filed solely with a request for reduction, the judge cannot completely abolish alimony/maintenance ex officio without amendment or counterclaim. The reverse is possible: in a case filed with a request for abolishment, if the judge sees that the conditions are not fully met, they can reduce the alimony/maintenance on the principle of "the lesser is included in the greater."

lines: Case Summary Mr. Serkan and Ms. Ayşe divorced by agreement in 2019; according to the protocol, Mr. Serkan agreed to pay a monthly spousal support alimony/maintenance of 6,000 TL to Ms. Ayşe, who was not working, and a monthly child support alimony/maintenance of 4,000 TL for their common child. Within six years, both inflation and Mr. Serkan's income tripled with a promotion, while the alimony/maintenance amount never changed.

lines: Trial and Proof Process Ms. Ayşe filed a lawsuit for an increase in alimony/maintenance in the family court through her lawyer. New salary slips of Mr. Serkan and an SGK service breakdown related to the change of title were presented as evidence in the petition, and the six-year CPI increase was reported by an expert. Mr. Serkan partially objected by presenting evidence of his new maintenance obligation arising from his new marriage and increased expenses. The court rendered its decision on the fourth hearing after evaluating the expert report.

lines: Legal Ruling The court ruled that Mr. Serkan's income increase should be reflected in Ms. Ayşe's and the child's standard of living, but also that Mr. Serkan's new maintenance obligation should be taken into account for fairness. Spousal support alimony/maintenance was increased from 6,000 TL to 11,000 TL, and child support alimony/maintenance from 4,000 TL to 8,500 TL; it was ruled that it should be automatically increased annually by the PPI rate every January.

lines: Frequently Asked Questions
nafaka-turleri-ve-artirim-azaltim-davasi.text: Frequently Asked Questions

lines: Does spousal support alimony/maintenance automatically end if the ex-spouse remarries? In case of remarriage with an official marriage, spousal support alimony/maintenance automatically terminates by law; enforcement proceedings can be stopped without the need for a separate abolishment lawsuit.
nafaka-turleri-ve-artirim-azaltim-davasi.text: Does spousal support alimony/maintenance automatically end if the ex-spouse remarries? In case of remarriage with an official marriage, spousal support alimony/maintenance automatically terminates by law; enforcement proceedings can be stopped without the need for a separate abolishment lawsuit.

lines: In contrast, cohabitation with another person without an official marriage does not automatically produce results; this situation must be proven in court and terminated by a lawsuit for the abolishment of alimony/maintenance.
nafaka-turleri-ve-artirim-azaltim-davasi.text: In contrast, cohabitation with another person without an official marriage does not automatically produce results; this situation must be proven in court and terminated by a lawsuit for the abolishment of alimony/maintenance.

lines: Can indefinite alimony/maintenance payments be stopped immediately after the 2026 Constitutional Court decision? No. Although the decision annulled the phrase "indefinitely," the entry into force of this annulment has been postponed for 9 months from its publication in the Official Gazette. During this period, the current legal provision and finalized alimony/maintenance decisions remain valid. Unilaterally stopping payments before the effective date carries the risk of enforcement proceedings and disciplinary imprisonment. Even when the effective date arrives, the time limit will not automatically arise; it will be clarified by a new regulation by the Turkish Grand National Assembly or by an adaptation lawsuit to be filed.

During this period, the current legal provision and finalized alimony/maintenance decisions remain valid. Unilaterally stopping payments before the effective date carries the risk of enforcement proceedings and disciplinary imprisonment. Even when the effective date arrives, the time limit will not automatically arise; it will be clarified by a new regulation by the Turkish Grand National Assembly or by an adaptation lawsuit to be filed.

lines: Is imprisonment applied if alimony/maintenance debt cannot be paid? The Enforcement and Bankruptcy Law (İİK) provides for disciplinary imprisonment for debtors who intentionally do not pay alimony/maintenance debt; however, this sanction is applied when the debt is not paid culpably and intentionally. A debtor who proves that their payment capacity has objectively ceased due to unavoidable reasons such as unemployment or health problems can both object in the enforcement court and file a lawsuit for the reduction or temporary suspension of alimony/maintenance in the family court.

lines: Does child support alimony/maintenance automatically stop when the child turns 18? Child support alimony/maintenance automatically terminates by law on the date the child becomes an adult, and there is no need for a separate abolishment lawsuit. If the child continues their education, they can request alimony/maintenance for the duration of their education by filing a separate assistance alimony/maintenance lawsuit on their own behalf.

lines: Attention: Common Procedural Errors Wrong type of lawsuit selection: Asking for abolishment verbally at the hearing after filing a lawsuit solely for reduction; this will not be taken into account by the judge because a proper amendment or counterclaim was not made.

lines: Filing a lawsuit without or with insufficient evidence: Stating that income has increased is not enough; lawsuits filed without concrete documents are rejected due to insufficient evidence. Unilaterally stopping alimony/maintenance: Stopping payments without a court decision leads to enforcement proceedings and disciplinary imprisonment.

lines: Filing a lawsuit in the wrong court: An increase/decrease lawsuit must be filed in the family court of the defendant's domicile, not the court that rendered the divorce decision; otherwise, loss of time and fees will occur due to a decision of incompetence or lack of jurisdiction.

lines: Failure to include an index clause: If the annual increase rate is not specified in the decision, alimony/maintenance loses its real value against inflation and a new lawsuit must be filed each time.

lines: Conclusion Alimony/maintenance law is a dynamic field strictly tied to the personal economic conditions of the parties, the duration of the marriage, and the new legislation that will be shaped after the Constitutional Court's decision in 2026. Just as formulating the initial alimony/maintenance request in the correct type and amount is crucial, supporting a subsequent increase or decrease lawsuit with concrete evidence plays a decisive role in a favorable outcome of the process.

lines: Summary Establishing an organization to commit a crime is an independent offense regulated under Article 220 of the Turkish Penal Code, punishable even if the intended crimes have not yet been committed. For a structure to be considered an organization, it must cumulatively meet the conditions of having at least three people, a hierarchical link, continuity, and means suitable for the purpose. Establishing an organization is punishable by 4-8 years of imprisonment, and membership by 2-4 years. In contrast, Article 221 of the Turkish Penal Code offers immunity from punishment or a significant reduction for genuinely cooperative perpetrators, depending on the organization's status.

lines: Why does a structure lead to punishment even without a crime being committed? The most common misconception in organized crime is the belief that "no crime has been committed yet, so there won't be any punishment." However, the Turkish Penal Code considers the establishment of an organization as a danger in itself and punishes those who establish, manage, and are members of the organization, even if the intended crimes are not committed. This situation creates a critical knowledge gap both for individuals involved in the process as suspects and for those considering leaving the organization.

lines: What is the Offense of Establishing an Organization to Commit a Crime? Article 220 of the Turkish Penal Code considers public peace as the protected legal value. The legislator punishes the mere establishment of a suitable structure for this purpose, independently of the crimes the perpetrators ultimately aim to commit. In this respect, the offense is an abstract danger crime that punishes the likelihood of harm occurring, rather than the occurrence of concrete harm. The moment an organization meeting the elements required by law is established, those who establish, manage, and join the organization are held responsible, even if the intended crimes (e.g., drug trafficking, robbery, or fraud) have not yet been committed at all.

lines: Conditions for a Structure to be Considered an Organization In line with doctrine and the decisions of the Grand Chamber of Criminal Cases of the Court of Cassation, for an ordinary association or complicity relationship to be considered a criminal organization, the following four elements must cumulatively exist.
orgutlu-suclar-ve-etkin-pismanlik.text: Conditions for a Structure to be Considered an Organization In line with doctrine and the decisions of the Grand Chamber of Criminal Cases of the Court of Cassation, for an ordinary association or complicity relationship to be considered a criminal organization, the following four elements must cumulatively exist.

lines: At least three persons: The presence of at least three real persons, including founders, managers, and members, is essential. Two people coming together do not constitute an organization in the sense of criminal law. Hierarchical link: There must be a superior-subordinate or command-control relationship among the members, even if loose.

lines: Structures that do not include hierarchy and consist only of horizontal cooperation are not considered organizations. Continuity and uncertainty: When individuals come together to commit only a single concrete crime and then disperse, it is a relationship of complicity. For an organization to be spoken of, the structure must exhibit continuity and be established around the purpose of committing an indeterminate number of crimes that have not yet materialized.

lines: Suitability of means and equipment: The number of members, logistics capabilities, and equipment possessed by the structure must be concretely suitable for committing the intended crimes. The fundamental difference between complicity and an organization is this: in complicity, perpetrators come together to commit a specific crime, and the association ends with the execution of the crime. In an organization, complicity is not tied to a concrete act; it is continuous over time and has an independent existence.

lines: Making propaganda for the organization m.220/8 1-3 years imprisonment (increases if committed through the press) In accordance with the actual concurrence rule applicable in our criminal law, penalties given for establishing, managing, or being a member of an organization are independent of the penalties for other underlying crimes (such as robbery, drug manufacturing, qualified fraud) committed within the framework of the organization's activities. Perpetrators are punished separately for both the organization crime and each crime they commit. Furthermore, according to the fifth paragraph of Article 220 of the Turkish Penal Code, organization managers are held responsible as perpetrators for all crimes committed within the scope of the organization's activities, even if they did not personally participate in the executive actions.

lines: Difference Between a Criminal Organization and a Terrorist Organization The most commonly confused issue in practice is the distinction between an ordinary criminal organization (Turkish Penal Code m.220) and a terrorist organization (m.314). Classic criminal organizations are generally established to gain illicit economic profit or regional influence. Terrorist organizations, on the other hand, act with political, ideological, or religious motives, aiming to change the constitutional order of the state or disrupt the country's integrity. The basic penalty for membership in a terrorist organization is 5-10 years imprisonment, and these penalties are increased by half in accordance with Article 5 of the Anti-Terror Law. Detention periods, limits on pre-trial detention, and confidentiality orders in terror crimes are also applied much more strictly than for ordinary criminal organizations.

lines: Effective Remorse: Why Does the Justice System "Reward" It? Effective remorse is a ground for impunity or reduction of punishment applied when the perpetrator, after the completion of the crime, shows remorse and takes steps to limit the negative consequences of the crime. The state, in its struggle against organized crime, promises a legal quid pro quo for genuine cooperation, aiming to dismantle the structure from within. Article 221 of the Turkish Penal Code regulates four different possibilities depending on the perpetrator's role.

lines: For Founders and Managers: Self-Dissolution If the person who founded or managed the organization personally dissolves the organization before the intended crimes begin to be committed, or ensures its dissolution with the information they provide, they will not be punished for the organization crime.

lines: Voluntary Withdrawal Before Apprehension If an organization member, without participating in the commission of any underlying crime, voluntarily informs the authorities of their withdrawal from the organization and expresses remorse, they will not be punished for membership.

lines: Contribution to the Dismantling of the Organization After Apprehension If an organization member who has not been involved in any crime, shows remorse after being apprehended and provides concrete information suitable for ensuring the dissolution of the organization or the apprehension of other members, they will also not be punished.
orgutlu-suclar-ve-etkin-pismanlik.text: Contribution to the Dismantling of the Organization After Apprehension If an organization member who has not been involved in any crime, shows remorse after being apprehended and provides concrete information suitable for ensuring the dissolution of the organization or the apprehension of other members, they will also not be punished.

lines: Providing Information About Committed Crimes Whether or not the perpetrator has committed a crime within the organization; if they spontaneously surrender before apprehension and provide information about the structure of the organization and the committed crimes, they will not be punished. If they provide genuine information after apprehension, a reduction of one-third to three-fourths will be applied to the punishment for the crime of establishing, managing, or being a member of the organization.

lines: Procedural Rules for Effective Remorse According to the established decisions of the Court of Cassation, abstract, generally known statements are not sufficient for the defendant to benefit from effective remorse. The information provided must be concrete enough to reveal the code names, true identities, meeting places of other members, or previously concealed actions, and effective enough to change the course of the investigation.

lines: There is no legal limit stating that an effective remorse statement can only be made during the police or prosecutor's investigation phase. The perpetrator can request the application of effective remorse provisions by making genuine confessions during the first instance court process, or even at the appeal or cassation stage after a conviction, until the judgment becomes final.

According to the law, a supervised release measure is applied to these persons for a period of 1 year from the date of their release; the court may extend this period up to 3 years depending on the perpetrator's situation.

lines: Legal Evaluation The structure is considered a criminal organization under Article 220 of the Turkish Penal Code in terms of member count, hierarchical division of tasks, continuity, and means suitable for the purpose (fake identities, accounts). However, the person providing the information will not be punished for membership under the second paragraph of Article 221 of the Turkish Penal Code, because they voluntarily reported to the authorities before the underlying crimes were committed, and the information they provided led to the dissolution of the organization. The other members will be prosecuted within the framework of establishing an organization or membership provisions, depending on their situation.

lines: Can I benefit from effective remorse if I don't tell anyone I left the organization? No. To benefit from effective remorse provisions, the intention to leave must be reported to the competent authorities (police or prosecutor). Silently withdrawing does not produce a legal result.

lines: What happens if the information I provide after being apprehended is not useful? The information provided must be concrete and verifiable enough to advance the investigation. General statements that can even be found by an internet search are not considered sufficient for effective remorse, and no reduction will be applied.

lines: Summary The right to be forgotten is an individual's right to prevent adverse news or a judicial matter from the past that has lost its current relevance from remaining indefinitely accessible on the internet. Unlike removal of the news from its source, this right is generally exercised by de-indexing it from the search engine. Three separate avenues may be pursued: a direct application to Google; if rejected, a complaint to the Personal Data Protection Board; or an application to the Criminal Judgeship of Peace.

lines: The News Was Accurate, So Why Does It Still Appear First? An event that occurred years ago and was accurately reported at the time may continue to appear when a person's name is searched, despite the passage of time. The accuracy of the news is not in dispute; the issue is whether that information still has value that warrants public awareness today.

lines: The Difference Between Removing Content and De-indexing It from a Search Engine The issue most frequently misunderstood in digital reputation management is the distinction between removing content from a website and removing a link from a search engine. Removing content at its source means completely deleting the infringing material from the server of the website on which it was published; in that event, the content will also disappear from search engines automatically, although local newspapers or digital archives may not always accept such requests. De-indexing from a search engine means that the news remains on the website but is not listed when the person's name is searched. This second method constitutes the essence of the right to be forgotten; freedom of the press is thus not entirely restricted, while the individual is able to protect his or her digital identity.

lines: Mr. Ahmet, an architect, was prosecuted in 2012 on charges of breach of trust arising from a commercial dispute, and the proceedings concluded with his acquittal in 2015. Despite the many years that have elapsed, news reports from 2012 continue to appear first when his name is searched. This makes it difficult for him to secure new business projects.

lines: Legal Assessment The fact that the proceedings concluded with an acquittal and the substantial period that has elapsed satisfy the conditions for the right to be forgotten. By documenting the acquittal judgment and the passage of time, Mr. Ahmet may request that these results be removed from the search engine.

lines: Procedure for Removing a Name from Google Search Results Since the vast majority of internet searches are conducted through Google, the process generally focuses on this platform. First, Google's official application form entitled “Removal of Search Results under Personal Data Protection Legislation” must be completed. The URLs requested to be removed must be added individually and in full; the exact first-name and surname combination used for the search must be specified; the reasons why the content should be removed must be explained by reference to the above criteria; and supporting documents, such as a court judgment, must be uploaded in PDF format.

lines: When reviewing the application, Google's legal team applies a balancing test between freedom of expression and personality rights. If the application is found justified, the relevant links are removed from name-based searches; if it is rejected, legal remedies must be pursued.

lines: What Remedies Are Available If Google Rejects the Request? Since search engines are commercial companies, there is always a possibility that they may reject applications. In that event, two separate legal avenues are available. Under Law No. 6698, search engines are deemed data controllers and indexing activity is deemed data processing. If the application submitted to Google is rejected or no response is provided within 30 days, the individual may lodge a complaint with the Personal Data Protection Board. If the Board determines that the criteria for the right to be forgotten are satisfied, it issues binding instructions directing the search engine to de-index the content.

lines: Another avenue is to apply directly to the Criminal Judgeship of Peace having jurisdiction over the applicant's place of residence. The petition must explain in concrete terms that the appearance of the applicant's name in search results infringes his or her personality rights and that the conditions for the right to be forgotten have arisen. If the Judgeship finds the request justified, it orders the content to be removed from the search engine's index; this avenue generally provides the fastest outcome.

lines: Circumstances May an Action for Reduction Be Brought? A practical guide to the reserved-share regime and actions for reduction under Articles 505–507 and 560–571 of the Turkish Civil Code. This guide has been prepared on the basis of the provisions of the Turkish Civil Code in force as of 2026 and current Court of Cassation practice.
sakli-pay-ve-tenkis-davasi-rehberi.text: Circumstances May an Action for Reduction Be Brought? A practical guide to the reserved-share regime and actions for reduction under Articles 505–507 and 560–571 of the Turkish Civil Code. This guide has been prepared on the basis of the provisions of the Turkish Civil Code in force as of 2026 and current Court of Cassation practice.

lines: Under Turkish law, a testator is free to dispose of their assets as they wish by will or inheritance contract; however, this freedom is not unlimited. The law protects the testator’s closest relatives—their descendants, parents, and surviving spouse—through a safeguard known as the reserved share and prevents the testator from encroaching upon such shares. If the testator has donated or bequeathed to a third party or an heir an amount exceeding the reserved shares, a reserved-share heir whose rights have been infringed may, after the testator’s death, bring an action for reduction and request that the disposition be reduced to the statutory limit. As an action for reduction is subject to strict legal requirements, a mandatory order of reduction, and limitation periods resulting in forfeiture of rights, conducting the proceedings with the guidance of legal counsel ensures both that the proper party is sued for the correct amount and that the applicable period is not missed.

lines: 1. What Is a Reserved Share? A reserved share is the proportion of an inheritance that, pursuant to Articles 505 and 506 of the Turkish Civil Code, must by law be allocated to certain heirs and over which the testator may not freely dispose. The testator may freely dispose by will or inheritance contract only of the disposable portion of the estate remaining after the reserved shares have been deducted. A disposition infringing a reserved share is not automatically deemed invalid; the reserved-share heir may either accept the situation or bring an action for reduction to seek rectification of the infringement.

lines: 2. Reserved-Share Heirs and Reserved-Share Ratios Pursuant to Article 506 of the Turkish Civil Code, reserved-share heirs are the testator’s descendants, parents, and surviving spouse. Following the legislative amendment enacted in 2007, siblings ceased to be reserved-share heirs; the testator may completely eliminate their siblings’ inheritance rights through a testamentary disposition. The reserved-share ratio is calculated by first determining the heir’s statutory share and then applying the ratio prescribed by law to that share.

lines: 3. Dispositions Subject to Reduction The subject matter of an action for reduction consists primarily of testamentary dispositions made by the testator through a will or inheritance contract. In addition, to prevent circumvention of the reserved-share regime through inter vivos transactions, Article 565 of the Turkish Civil Code subjects certain gratuitous dispositions to reduction in the same manner as testamentary dispositions: dispositions made on account of an inheritance share to a statutory heir who subsequently loses heirship status; transfers of assets to descendants or releases of descendants from debts without being subject to restitution; dowries and start-up capital provided beyond customary limits; dispositions made for the purpose of settling inheritance rights before death; and donations made by the testator while reserving an unrestricted right of revocation. By contrast, transactions for which consideration has been paid, such as a genuine sale or a contract for lifelong care in return for consideration, fall outside the scope of reduction. If it is alleged that such transactions in fact conceal a donation, the relevant action is not an action for reduction but an action based on fraudulent conveyance by the decedent.

lines: 4. Requirements for an Action for Reduction Two fundamental requirements must be satisfied concurrently for an action for reduction to be brought: the testator must have exceeded the disposable portion through a testamentary disposition or an inter vivos disposition subject to reduction, and that excess must have actually infringed the claimant heir’s reserved share. The disposable portion is determined by deducting the aggregate reserved shares from the entire estate; the testator may freely dispose only of the remaining portion. An action for reduction cannot be brought while the testator is alive; even where a transaction infringing the reserved share is known with certainty to have been effected, the right of action arises only upon the testator’s death.

lines: 5. Who May Bring an Action for Reduction, and Against Whom? An action for reduction may be brought only by a reserved-share heir whose reserved share has been infringed; heirs without a reserved share or heirs whose reserved share has not been infringed may not bring such an action. Each reserved-share heir has a separate and independent right of action. If only one heir brings the action, the court’s reduction judgment produces consequences solely for the claimant heir and does not bind the other reserved-share heirs.

lines: Exceptionally, creditors of a reserved-share heir may also bring an action for reduction subject to certain conditions. The action is brought against the person benefiting from the disposition that infringes the reserved share—the legatee or the third-party donee.

lines: 6. Court with Subject-Matter and Territorial Jurisdiction; Time Limits The Civil Court of First Instance has subject-matter jurisdiction over actions for reduction, while the court of the testator’s last place of residence has territorial jurisdiction. Pursuant to Article 571 of the Turkish Civil Code, the action is subject to limitation periods resulting in forfeiture of rights: an heir whose reserved share has been infringed must bring the action within one year from the date on which the heir learns of the impairment of the reserved share and the disposition subject to reduction. In any event, the period is ten years from the date on which the will is opened where the infringement is based on a will, and from the date of the testator’s death in the case of inter vivos dispositions. The court considers these periods ex officio; the defendant need not raise a time-bar objection.

The amount stated in the statement of claim is an estimated value serving as the basis for court fees and is determined precisely during the proceedings through an expert examination. Due to this characteristic, an action for reduction is treated in practice as an action for an unquantified claim.

lines: 7. Order of Reduction Where there is more than one disposition subject to reduction, Article 570 of the Turkish Civil Code governs which disposition is to be reduced first. Accordingly, reduction is first applied to testamentary dispositions until the reserved share is restored; if this is insufficient, reduction continues with inter vivos dispositions in reverse chronological order, from the most recent to the oldest. Testamentary and inter vivos dispositions made in favor of public legal entities and associations and foundations serving the public interest are reduced last. Where there is more than one beneficiary of testamentary dispositions, such dispositions are reduced proportionately among them; if the testator has expressed a contrary intention, that intention is given priority.

lines: 8. Difference Between an Action for Reduction and an Action Based on Fraudulent Conveyance by the Decedent These two actions, which are frequently confused in practice, are based on different legal grounds. In an action for reduction, the disposition made by the testator is legally valid; the action seeks only to reduce the portion of that valid disposition exceeding the reserved share to the statutory limit. In an action based on fraudulent conveyance by the decedent, it is alleged that the ostensible transaction—for example, a sale—does not reflect the parties’ true intention and conceals a disguised donation made to deprive heirs of inherited property; a declaration that the transaction is entirely invalid is sought. In practice, these two actions may be brought together in the alternative as successive claims: the court first considers the allegation of simulation and, if it rejects that allegation, then considers the claim for reduction.

lines: CASE SUMMARY FORM Mr. Nihat, a retired teacher, left his sole immovable property in Istanbul to Deniz, the youngest of his three children, by an official will executed two years before his death. After their father’s death, when the other two children, Ayşe and Kemal, obtained the certificate of inheritance, they discovered that virtually no assets remained in the estate other than the immovable property.
sakli-pay-ve-tenkis-davasi-rehberi.text: CASE SUMMARY FORM Mr. Nihat, a retired teacher, left his sole immovable property in Istanbul to Deniz, the youngest of his three children, by an official will executed two years before his death. After their father’s death, when the other two children, Ayşe and Kemal, obtained the certificate of inheritance, they discovered that virtually no assets remained in the estate other than the immovable property.

lines: APPLICATION AND LEGAL PROCEEDINGS Counsel for Ayşe and Kemal first determined that all three children were reserved-share heirs as descendants and that each child’s reserved share corresponded to one-half of their statutory share. As the bequest of the entire immovable property to Deniz clearly infringed Ayşe’s and Kemal’s reserved shares, an action for reduction was brought before the Civil Court of First Instance at the testator’s last place of residence. In the statement of claim, determination of the immovable property’s current value was left to expert examination, and the court fee was paid on the basis of an estimated amount. lines: Consequences A practical guide to actual disclaimer, deemed disclaimer, and the legal consequences of disclaimer under Articles 605–618 of the Turkish Civil Code. This guide has been prepared on the basis of the provisions of the Turkish Civil Code in force as of 2026 and current Court of Cassation practice.
reddi-miras-nasil-yapilir-rehberi.text: Consequences A practical guide to actual disclaimer, deemed disclaimer, and the legal consequences of disclaimer under Articles 605–618 of the Turkish Civil Code. This guide has been prepared on the basis of the provisions of the Turkish Civil Code in force as of 2026 and current Court of Cassation practice.

lines: Under Turkish law, an inheritance passes to the heirs automatically and as a whole upon the decedent's death; this transfer encompasses not only the assets but also the decedent's debts. An heir is not obliged to accept the inheritance: the heir may disclaim it unconditionally by applying to the court within three months. Furthermore, where the estate was manifestly insolvent at the date of death, the inheritance is deemed disclaimed automatically without any declaration being required; this second avenue is known as deemed disclaimer. The procedure, time limit, and burden of proof differ for each avenue; choosing the wrong avenue or missing the deadline may result in the heir being held liable for the decedent's debts out of the heir's own assets.

lines: 1. What Is Disclaimer of Inheritance? Disclaimer of inheritance is the act whereby a statutory or appointed heir declares that the heir does not wish to accept the rights and obligations passing to the heir upon the decedent's death and is thereby released from the consequences of heirship. Pursuant to Article 605/1 of the Turkish Civil Code, both statutory and appointed heirs may disclaim an inheritance. Since, under the principle of universal succession, the decedent's debts also form part of the estate, disclaimer of inheritance is a fundamental protective mechanism that safeguards an heir from being held liable out of the heir's personal assets, particularly where the estate is indebted.

lines: 2. Distinction Between Actual Disclaimer and Deemed Disclaimer The law regulates disclaimer of inheritance in two different forms. Actual disclaimer occurs where the heir, by an active exercise of will, disclaims the inheritance through an express declaration addressed to the court, and it is subject to a three-month forfeiture period. Deemed disclaimer occurs where the decedent's insolvency at the date of death was manifest or officially established, in which case the inheritance is deemed disclaimed automatically without the heir being required to make a separate declaration (Article 605/2 of the Turkish Civil Code). Although both avenues seek the same result—namely, that the heir is not held liable for the decedent's debts—their procedural and evidentiary requirements are entirely different.

lines: 3. How and Where Is an Actual Disclaimer Made? Pursuant to Article 609 of the Turkish Civil Code, an actual disclaimer of inheritance is effected by an oral or written declaration made by the heir to the Civil Court of Peace at the decedent's last place of residence. The declaration must be unconditional; a declaration of disclaimer subject to any condition is invalid. The Civil Judge of Peace records the declaration in official minutes, and a disclaimer made within the prescribed period is entered in the special register of the court at the place where the inheritance opened. Upon request, the disclaiming heir is also issued a document evidencing this status. A declaration of disclaimer made before a notary public or another court is legally invalid and does not result in disclaimer of the inheritance.

lines: 4. Disclaimer Period and Its Commencement The three-month period prescribed for an actual disclaimer is a forfeiture period and is taken into account by the court ex officio; it is neither suspended nor interrupted. The commencement date varies according to the heir's status: for statutory heirs, the period generally begins on the date they learn of the decedent's death. If the status as heir is learned at a later date, or if the heir was excluded from the inheritance by a disposition upon death that was subsequently annulled, the period runs from the date of such discovery or annulment. For appointed heirs, the period begins on the date the will is officially opened by the Civil Court of Peace and served upon them. Where an inventory of the estate is drawn up as a protective measure, this period is reduced to one month and begins on the date the invitation issued by the Civil Court of Peace preparing the inventory is served upon the heir (Article 626 of the Turkish Civil Code).

lines: Inheritance Law Series If, at the date of the decedent's death, it was manifest that the decedent's debts exceeded the assets, or if this circumstance had been officially established, the inheritance is deemed disclaimed automatically pursuant to Article 605/2 of the Turkish Civil Code; no separate declaration of disclaimer is required. In practice, however, it is highly advisable for heirs to bring an “action for a declaration of deemed disclaimer of inheritance” so that they have a definitive legal basis against future enforcement proceedings and actions brought by estate creditors. This is a declaratory action seeking a determination that the estate is insolvent; according to the settled case law of the Court of Cassation, the competent court is the Civil Court of First Instance irrespective of the value in dispute, and the action must be brought against the estate creditors; uncontested applications may be dismissed for failure to name an opposing party. An action for deemed disclaimer is not subject to any time limit, and deemed disclaimer may also be raised at any time as a defence in enforcement proceedings or actions initiated by estate creditors.

lines: 6. Consequences of Disclaimer An heir who validly disclaims the inheritance is treated as though the heir had predeceased the decedent; the disclaimer produces consequences only for the disclaiming heir and does not affect the inheritance rights of the heir's descendants. Pursuant to Article 611 of the Turkish Civil Code, the share disclaimed by a statutory heir passes to the other heirs—for example, to the disclaiming child's own children (the decedent's grandchildren)—as though the disclaiming heir had predeceased the decedent. If all statutory heirs in the nearest order of succession disclaim the inheritance, the estate is liquidated by the Civil Judge of Peace in accordance with the provisions governing bankruptcy pursuant to Article 612 of the Turkish Civil Code; if any surplus remains after the debts are paid upon completion of the liquidation, that surplus is paid to the heirs who disclaimed the inheritance. Thus, the heirs are both protected from the debts and entitled to receive a share of any positive value remaining in the estate.

lines: 7. Loss of the Right to Disclaim: Implied Acceptance Pursuant to Article 610 of the Turkish Civil Code, an heir who interferes in the affairs of the estate, carries out transactions exceeding ordinary administration, or conceals or appropriates estate property before the disclaimer period expires may no longer disclaim the inheritance; such conduct is regarded as implied acceptance. For example, using a vehicle belonging to the decedent, leasing an immovable belonging to the estate, or attempting to sell it may result in loss of the right to disclaim.

lines: 8. Disclaimer of Inheritance on Behalf of Minors and Persons Under Guardianship A declaration of disclaimer on behalf of persons entirely lacking capacity to act is made by their legal representatives (parent exercising custody or guardian). In the case of minors, provided there is no conflict of interest between the parent and the minor, the declaration of disclaimer may be made through parental representation; if a potential conflict of interest exists, the court may appoint a trustee for the minor. For heirs under guardianship, in addition to the guardian's declaration, authorisation must be obtained from the guardianship authority (the Civil Court of Peace) and, where necessary, the supervisory authority (the Civil Court of First Instance). Since these authorisation procedures may take time, the three-month period must be monitored carefully from the outset when applying for disclaimer on behalf of minors or persons under guardianship.

lines: 9. Annulment of Disclaimer and Protection of Creditors The law provides protection for creditors against the possibility that an heir may disclaim an inheritance with the intention of prejudicing the decedent's creditors. Pursuant to Article 617 of the Turkish Civil Code, if an heir's disclaimer prejudices the estate creditors, those creditors or the bankruptcy administration may bring an action for annulment of the disclaimer within six months of the date of disclaimer. If the court finds that the heir acted in bad faith, it will annul the disclaimer; in that event, the estate is liquidated in accordance with the provisions governing bankruptcy, and any surplus remaining after liquidation is paid first to the creditors who brought the action. Furthermore, if the heir's own declaration of disclaimer was made as a result of mistake, fraud, or duress, it may separately be challenged by an action for annulment under the general provisions of the Turkish Code of Obligations.
